title: Implement /optimize/suggestions API endpoint with pagination, sorting, and stable IDs
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
## Summary
Console needs a production-safe Suggestions list endpoint for the Optimize Suggestions beta. Implement `GET /optimize/suggestions` with:
- server-side pagination
- deterministic sorting
- stable suggestion IDs (so UI can cache, deep-link, and reconcile across refreshes)
- strict org/project scoping + RBAC enforcement

This endpoint is consumed by the Console Suggestions view (table + details drawer). The API must be resilient to compute job lag/staleness and must not leak data across tenants.

## Goals / Requirements
### API surface
- Endpoint: `GET /optimize/suggestions`
- Scope: Suggestions for the current org + project context (as derived from auth token + request path/headers per Console conventions)
- Return a list of suggestion summaries suitable for table display + a stable identifier for fetching details.

### Pagination
- Must support cursor-based pagination (preferred) or offset-based with stable ordering guarantees.
- Support `limit` with enforced max (see perf budget notes below).
- Response must include `next_cursor` (or equivalent) and be safe under new suggestion inserts.

### Sorting
Support `sort_by` and `sort_dir`.
Required sort keys for beta:
- `estimated_savings_usd_per_day` (desc default)
- `estimated_savings_pct`
- `risk_level` (with defined ordering Low < Medium < High)
- `confidence` (desc)
- `updated_at` / `computed_at` (desc)

Sorting must be deterministic. Tie-break using stable ID to ensure consistent pagination.

### Stable IDs
- Each suggestion must have a stable ID that is unchanged across recomputation as long as the underlying “target” is the same.
- Proposed identity components (per ADR): org_id + project_id + suggestion_type + route_id + model_id (+ region if suggestions are region-scoped).
- The stable ID must be opaque to the client (string). If we use a hash, include version prefix (e.g., `sug_v1_...`) to allow future changes.

### Filtering (MVP)
Support filter parameters needed by Console UX (beta):
- `route_id` (exact)
- `model_id` (exact)
- `suggestion_type` (enum: `batching`, `caching`)
- `risk_level` (enum)

### Staleness
- Return `stale_as_of` (timestamp) or `computed_at` for each suggestion; UI will show “Estimates updated X hours ago”.
- If compute is behind, endpoint should still respond quickly with last known data.

### Error handling
- 401/403 for auth/RBAC failures.
- 400 for invalid parameters (unknown sort keys, invalid cursor, invalid enums).
- 429 if rate limited.
- 5xx only for unexpected server errors. Log with request_id + org_id.

## Non-goals
- Creating the estimator logic (handled in ENG-19419).
- Auto-applying suggestions.
- Exposing the full “details drawer” object in the list endpoint beyond what’s needed for the table (details endpoint may come later; for beta, list can include enough fields for drawer if payload remains within budget).

## Proposed response fields (beta)
Return fields needed for list + initial details drawer:
- `suggestion_id` (stable)
- `suggestion_type` (`batching` | `caching`)
- `target_route_id`, `target_route_name`
- `target_model_id`, `target_model_name`
- `region` (optional; include empty string if not applicable)
- `estimated_savings_usd_per_day`
- `estimated_savings_pct`
- `estimated_p50_latency_delta_ms`, `estimated_p95_latency_delta_ms`
- `risk_level` (`low` | `medium` | `high`)
- `confidence` (0–1 as string/decimal; UI renders as High/Med/Low)
- `computed_at` and/or `stale_as_of`
- `explanation_summary` (1–2 sentences)
- `recommended_config` (for beta, may be a short string blob; if too large, keep a link-only approach)

Note: Keep payload size within the budget; avoid embedding large JSON configs in list responses.

## Perf / Reliability constraints
- p95 API latency target: <= 250ms under normal load for typical orgs.
- Payload size target: <= 200KB for default page size.
- Enforce max `limit` (e.g., 50) to control payload.
- Index to support default sort (`estimated_savings_usd_per_day desc`) and filter combinations.

## Implementation notes
- Data store: suggestions materialized table produced by compute job (see ENG-19455). This endpoint should be a thin query layer.
- Ensure deterministic ordering: `ORDER BY sort_key, suggestion_id`.
- Cursor encoding: base64 encode `(sort_key_value, suggestion_id)`; include sort key name + direction in cursor payload to prevent mismatched cursors after UI changes.
- Validate cursor against requested `sort_by` + `sort_dir`.
- RBAC: gate behind Optimize scope (see ENG-19377). Also ensure project boundary checks.
- Audit logging: log access to suggestions list (org_id, project_id, actor_id, count returned) but do NOT log full suggestion bodies.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Endpoint returns suggestions scoped to org+project and enforces RBAC.
- [x] Cursor pagination works with deterministic sorting and no duplicates across pages (under stable dataset).
- [x] Sorting supports required keys and matches Console expectations.
- [x] Stable IDs remain constant across recompute when target is unchanged.
- [x] Parameter validation returns 400 with actionable message.
- [x] Unit tests for cursor encode/decode + ordering; integration test for tenant isolation.
- [x] Basic metrics: request rate, latency, 4xx/5xx, payload size.

## Updates / Comments
2026-01-24 (Felix Schneider): Drafted API contract with Console team. Default sort: savings USD/day desc. Confirmed need for tie-breaker for pagination; will use `suggestion_id` as secondary sort.

2026-01-27 (Chloe Martin): Please ensure cursor is invalidated if sort params change. We had issues in other list endpoints where cursors were reused across sorts.

2026-01-30 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): RBAC scope name should align with new permission: `optimize:suggestions:read`. Add audit log event on successful read.

2026-02-02 (Felix Schneider): Implemented cursor encoding including sort key + dir + last seen values. Added max limit=50, default=20.

2026-02-04 (Dylan Brooks): UI wants `computed_at` at both item-level and response-level. If response-level is easier, include `stale_as_of` for the page as the max item computed_at.

2026-02-06 (Felix Schneider): Added response header `x-data-stale-as-of` (string timestamp) + item-level `computed_at`. Also added `risk_level` ordering map for sorting.

2026-02-10 (Marcus Lin): Security review: confirm no cross-tenant joins via route/model lookup tables. Ensure all lookups are constrained by org_id/project_id or use pre-joined denormalized fields.

2026-02-12 (Felix Schneider): Denormalized route_name/model_name in suggestions table to avoid cross-tenant joins. Added tests for org boundary.

2026-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Approved. Please ensure metrics include 403 counts to catch RBAC misconfiguration during beta.

## PRs
- GitHub: `pr-21934-add-optimize-suggestions-api-contract` (merged)

## Follow-ups
- Add details endpoint if/when the drawer grows beyond payload budget (TBD).
- Revisit indexes after beta telemetry (watch for slow sorts on confidence/risk).
- Add caching headers once we understand refresh cadence and staleness semantics.
